scope: Optical/environment gap audit. Recommendations are for the educational application, not a required bill of materials for any military spacecraft. Only directly opened primary sources are admitted. General practices, named civil hardware, ground support, and optional design choices remain distinct.

prioritizedAdditions.role: Let enclosed volumes vent while limiting contamination of sensitive surfaces
prioritizedAdditions.classification: representative flight-hardware detail supported by general practice
prioritizedAdditions.gap: The catalog contains housings and blankets but no vent-path explanation.
prioritizedAdditions.body: ECSS recommends directing instrument and blanket vents away from contamination-sensitive items. A representative cutaway can identify the housing opening and its routed passage.
row: Vents and blanket venting are directed away from sensitive items
prioritizedAdditions.implementation: Add a labeled passage in the representative housing, with geometry marked as drawn. Do not infer a mission vent count, dimension, filter, valve, or exact location.

prioritizedAdditions.role: Connect clean-gas ground support during integration and launch preparation
prioritizedAdditions.classification: ground-serviced instrument interface; not an onboard continuous purge system
prioritizedAdditions.gap: The current instrument story begins in space and omits its contamination-control service interface.
prioritizedAdditions.body: NASA's hosted-payload guidance separates the instrument's purge connection from the ground equipment that filters, conditions, and regulates the supplied gas.
row: A defined mechanical connection links instrument and ground purge equipment
prioritizedAdditions.implementation: Name the connection first; show ground tubing only in an integration inset. A schematic fitting is an assumption, not verified ABI or TIRS-2 geometry. Do not add flight gas tanks or pumps.

prioritizedAdditions.role: Set the detector relative to the telescope image plane during assembly
prioritizedAdditions.classification: named civil hardware; fixed adjustment established on the ground
prioritizedAdditions.gap: TIRS-2 has detector and electronics coverage but lacks a named alignment interface.
prioritizedAdditions.body: TIRS-2 subsystem optical tests supplied focus information for fabrication of alignment shims. These are fixed mechanical adjustments, not an on-orbit focusing actuator.
row: Ground focus measurements inform alignment-shim fabrication

refs: PDF p. 3, Section 4, first TIPCE paragraph

prioritizedAdditions.implementation: Add a thin schematic shim at a mounting interface. Do not invent shim material, thickness, number, stack-up, or detailed carrier geometry.

prioritizedAdditions.role: Select the thermal channels at the focal plane
prioritizedAdditions.gap: The TIRS-2 catalog mentions a filter assembly inside the baffles entry; the filters deserve their own identity near the arrays.
prioritizedAdditions.body: The TIRS-2 paper places interference filters over the detector arrays to select its spectral channels.
row: Interference filters over the arrays select the channels
prioritizedAdditions.implementation: Expose a separately labeled fixed filter element. Do not add a filter wheel or transfer ABI's beamsplitter architecture to TIRS-2.

groundSupportAndProcessAdditions.role: Protect sensitive surfaces during ground handling
groundSupportAndProcessAdditions.classification: ground support; separate from the existing flight optical-port cover
groundSupportAndProcessAdditions.body: NASA recommends protective covers and documented handling procedures during integration and testing.
row: Temporary covers protect sensitive instrument surfaces during integration and testing
groundSupportAndProcessAdditions.implementation: Ground-preparation inset only, with removal-before-flight status. Do not add another deployed flight door.

groundSupportAndProcessAdditions.componentName: Quartz crystal microbalance and residual gas analyzer
groundSupportAndProcessAdditions.role: Check deposition and residual gases during vacuum testing
groundSupportAndProcessAdditions.classification: test-facility hardware; not assumed flight equipment
groundSupportAndProcessAdditions.body: A microbalance measures accumulating material during vacuum tests. A residual gas analyzer helps identify the chamber's gaseous species. Flight contamination monitors are a separate mission-dependent choice.
row: Microbalance deposition measurements complement residual-gas analysis
groundSupportAndProcessAdditions.implementation: Add to Method or a testing inset. Do not inflate the spacecraft component count with chamber instrumentation.

groundSupportAndProcessAdditions.componentName: Adhesives, coatings, insulation, and harness materials
groundSupportAndProcessAdditions.role: Meet structural or electrical needs without excessive vacuum contamination
groundSupportAndProcessAdditions.body: NASA's materials standard calls for vacuum-stability screening and allows stricter evaluation near optical surfaces. Cold optics require particular attention to water deposition. Screening and bakeout are verification processes, not separate flight boxes.
row: Outgassing evaluation considers sensitive surfaces and cryogenic water deposition
groundSupportAndProcessAdditions.implementation: Annotate existing supports, insulation and wiring. Omit unsourced chemistry, numeric cleanliness thresholds, and mission-specific material selections.

groundSupportAndProcessAdditions.componentName: Calibration source, collimator, and steering mirror
groundSupportAndProcessAdditions.role: Illuminate the assembled civil instrument with characterized test inputs
groundSupportAndProcessAdditions.body: TIRS-2 characterization uses external calibration sources, a collimator, and steering optics. This equipment belongs to the test setup, not the flight telescope.
row: External calibration optics supply test illumination
groundSupportAndProcessAdditions.implementation: A Method diagram can distinguish ground calibration from the onboard blackbody already modeled.

coveredOrDoNotAdd.candidate: ABI outgas, survival, and operational heaters
coveredOrDoNotAdd.rationale: The current audited ledger already distinguishes these roles. Improve visibility or sublabels if needed; do not create a duplicate subsystem.

coveredOrDoNotAdd.candidate: Cryocooler, cold head, temperature sensor, cooler control and heat transport
coveredOrDoNotAdd.rationale: The architecture is present. A claimed new compressor interior, exact thermal-strap construction, or vibration-cancellation mechanism needs additional opened mission evidence.

coveredOrDoNotAdd.decision: do not add from this audit
coveredOrDoNotAdd.rationale: The thermal-paper access attempt was blocked. Search snippets are not evidence. The existing operational/survival heater entries remain the supported baseline.
The opened historical Landsat document concerns the original TIRS. Do not transfer hardware labels to TIRS-2 merely because it is a related instrument.

coveredOrDoNotAdd.candidate: Onboard purge tank, purge pump, universal vent filter or molecular adsorber
coveredOrDoNotAdd.rationale: General cleanliness guidance supports design evaluation and ground interfaces, not installation of these specific devices on the represented missions.
ECSS section 5.3.1.7 supports witness sampling during ground monitoring. It does not establish a flight witness-plate assembly.
row: Witness samples monitor molecular contamination in controlled environments

coveredOrDoNotAdd.candidate: Universal radiation vault or prescribed shielding thickness
coveredOrDoNotAdd.decision: do not add as required hardware
coveredOrDoNotAdd.rationale: NASA distinguishes shielding from existing spacecraft mass and optional local shielding. Particle energy and secondary production matter; thickness and layout need mission analysis.
row: Existing structure and optional local shields contribute differently to radiation protection

coveredOrDoNotAdd.candidate: Faraday cage, charge-dissipation coatings and bonding
coveredOrDoNotAdd.rationale: NASA-HDBK-4002B opened successfully; root owns the detailed charging proposal. Do not duplicate grounding or cable shields already in the catalog.
A representative uncrewed Earth-orbiting infrared observer does not inherit crewed or planetary-landing equipment from generic spacecraft literature.

productRecommendation: Add the three P1 physical/interface items with explicit applicability labels. Promote fixed TIRS-2 filters into a separately named component. Place materials and ground support in contextual details or a ground-preparation/testing inset. More independent flight boxes would weaken accuracy where sources only establish a process or an optional design choice.
checks: JSON validity only; no application edits, source-registry edits, builds, GPU tests, or publication performed by this audit.
